verdict.summary: Creating an OAuth app is self-serve, and flipping it to Public lets any workspace install it the same day with no documented review. The required config is the April 2026 refresh-token system (24-hour access tokens, rotating refresh tokens), and agent-style installs with actor=app need a workspace admin to approve them; the integration directory is optional and only for 'formal companies'.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create the app (optionally prefilled via a manifest URL), add a redirect URL, run the code flow against your own workspace.

timeToProd.assumes: A Public OAuth app using actor=app for an agent that reads and writes issues; each customer needs a workspace admin to install it. User-actor apps skip the admin step.
timeToProd.waitingOn: No review needed. Each customer's workspace admin for actor=app installs.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The manifest docs describe public distribution with no review step. The agents guide says admin permissions are required to complete an agent install.

prerequisites.item: A Linear workspace, ideally a dedicated one for owning the app
prerequisites.why: Linear recommends a separate workspace to manage the OAuth app, since each admin there has access to it.

prerequisites.item: Redirect callback URLs configured on the app
prerequisites.why: The redirect_uri in the token exchange must match the one used in the authorize request.
Access tokens last 24 hours and every refresh returns a new refresh token. All apps were moved to this system on April 1, 2026.

prerequisites.item: For agents: webhooks with Agent session events enabled
prerequisites.why: The Agents developer preview delivers delegation and mention events through webhooks.

scopeTiers.impact: Always included. Enough for an agent that searches and summarizes issues, projects and comments.
Narrow scopes cover creating issues or comments. write grants broad mutation access; Linear suggests a narrower scope when possible.
Lets users delegate issues to the agent and @mention it. A workspace admin has to complete the install. The APIs are a Developer Preview and may change.
Admin-level endpoints. Linear says to request it only when absolutely needed, and apps installed with actor=app can't request it.

steps.title: Create a dedicated workspace
steps.detail: Sign in and create (or pick) the workspace that will own the OAuth app.

steps.title: Draft the app manifest
steps.detail: Build a JSON manifest with the client name, redirect URLs, webhook settings and distribution: public, then URL-encode it into the manifest query parameter of the create page.

steps.title: Create the OAuth app
steps.detail: Open the prefilled create page, review it, toggle Public on, and save. Copy the client ID and secret.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: The create URL returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-20. We didn't sign in.

steps.title: Implement the authorization code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://linear.app/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, scope (comma-separated), state, and actor=app for agents. Add PKCE (S256) if you want. Exchange the code at https://api.linear.app/oauth/token.

steps.title: Handle refresh rotation
steps.detail: Refresh before the 24-hour expiry and save the new refresh token each time. If a refresh response is lost, replay the original request within the 30-minute grace period.

steps.title: Optional: wire up agent session webhooks
steps.detail: Enable Agent session events, request app:assignable and app:mentionable, and respond to delegation and mention events.

steps.title: Install into your own workspace
steps.detail: Authorize as a workspace admin and confirm the app appears and can act on issues.

steps.title: Launch to other workspaces
steps.detail: With Public on, share the Connect button. For actor=app, the customer's installer has to be a workspace admin.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: No review step is documented for public distribution.

steps.title: Optional: prepare the directory submission
steps.detail: Draft listing copy that follows the sample page, and prepare a 320px colour icon, a 320px white icon and 1–3 showcase images at 1600x1000.

steps.title: Optional: submit to the integration directory
steps.detail: Submit the form and send assets to integrations@linear.app. Linear accepts integrations it finds useful and built by formal companies.

agentCanDo: Write the OAuth app manifest and the prefilled create URL
Implement authorize, PKCE, token exchange and refresh rotation
Budget GraphQL complexity under the hourly limits
Draft directory copy and asset specs
humanMustDo: Sign in and create the app, toggling Public on
Install as a workspace admin to test actor=app
Get each customer's workspace admin to approve agent installs
Submit to the integration directory if listing

blockers.symptom: Users in other workspaces can't install the app
blockers.cause: Apps default to private distribution, which limits them to the creating workspace.
blockers.fix: Toggle Public on, or set distribution: public in the manifest.

blockers.symptom: Non-admin users can't finish installing the agent
blockers.cause: Admin permissions are required to complete an agent (actor=app) installation.
blockers.fix: Ask a workspace admin to install, or use the default user actor for per-user connections.

blockers.symptom: Token endpoint returns {"error":"invalid_client","error_description":"Invalid client: client is invalid"}
blockers.cause: Wrong client_id or client_secret, or a rotated secret.
blockers.fix: Re-copy the credentials from the app settings. Rotating the secret doesn't revoke existing access or refresh tokens.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed by POSTing dummy credentials to https://api.linear.app/oauth/token on 2026-10-20.

blockers.symptom: Connections break with invalid refresh token errors
blockers.cause: The app saved the old refresh token. Each refresh rotates it.
blockers.fix: Always store the newest refresh token, and replay within the 30-minute grace window if a response was lost.

blockers.cause: A single query can't exceed 10,000 complexity points, and OAuth apps get 2,000,000 points per hour per user or app user.
blockers.fix: Paginate with smaller page sizes and request fewer nested fields.

blockers.symptom: Requesting the admin scope fails for an agent install
blockers.cause: Apps installed with actor=app can't also request admin.
blockers.fix: Drop admin, or use a separate user-actor authorization for admin tasks.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 24 hours (expires_in 86399), and refresh tokens rotate on every use. All OAuth apps were migrated to this system on April 1, 2026.
OAuth apps get 5,000 requests and 2,000,000 complexity points per hour, counted per user or app user. For workspace-level actor=app installs, Linear raises limits based on the workspace's paid seats.
actor=app makes issues and comments appear as the app rather than the user. You can set a display name (createAsUser) and avatar (displayIconUrl) per mutation.
Installed agents don't count as billable users, and developing agents is free. The Agents APIs are a Developer Preview and may change before general availability.
Use prompt=consent to show the consent screen every time, which lets one user connect several workspaces.
Client-credentials tokens (app actor, 30 days, no refresh) exist for server-to-server use in your own workspace, with up to 1,000 active tokens per scope set.
